paper.title: Muon with Finite Newton-Schulz: The Smoothing Benefit in Nonsmooth Nonconvex Optimization
paper.abstract: Muon has emerged as a strong optimizer for the matrix-valued parameters in large language model pretraining, approximately orthogonalizing its momentum with a few Newton-Schulz iterations. Existing theory either replaces this iteration with the exact polar factor it approximates, or treats its finite depth as an approximation error, and thus the iteration Muon actually runs can only hurt the guarantees. summary.core_problem: 这篇论文解决 Muon 优化器理论中的一个关键缺口：真实 Muon 使用有限步 Newton–Schulz 迭代来近似动量矩阵的 polar factor，但已有理论要么直接分析 exact polar update，要么把有限迭代当作近似误差。作者证明，在非光滑非凸优化里，有限 Newton–Schulz 不是负担，而是能提供平滑性的关键机制。
summary.importance: 这篇论文对 LLM 预训练优化器研究有直接价值。Muon 已经在大规模预训练中表现出竞争力，核心操作是对矩阵参数的 momentum 做近似正交化。理论上，exact polar map 在奇异值接近 0 或秩变化处不连续，对应到 online learning 视角会退化为 operator-norm ball 上的 follow-the-leader，可能产生线性 regret，无法保证非光滑目标的 stationarity。论文指出，真实实现里“只做有限步 Newton–Schulz”反而把不连续的 polar map 变成奇异值上的 Lipschitz 映射，从而让 Muon with momentum 可以通过 online-to-nonconvex conversion 得到非光滑非凸 stationarity 保证。贡献量级不是给出一个新训练 recipe，而是解释了一个大规模预训练优化器中工程近似为何可能改善优化性质。
summary.technical_approach: 作者从 online-to-nonconvex conversion 进入分析。这个框架把优化器每一步的 update rule 看成一个 online learner，再把 learner 的 regret 转换为非光滑非凸目标上的 Goldstein-type stationarity 保证。对矩阵参数来说，Muon 的理想方向是 momentum 矩阵 M 的 polar factor：若 M = U Sigma V^T，则更新方向为 U V^T，相当于保留奇异向量、把所有正奇异值映射到 1。问题在于 exact polar map 是不连续的。有限 Newton–Schulz 使用固定奇多项式迭代，只需要矩阵乘法，不做 SVD；截断在 q 步后得到的映射不再是硬阈值式 polar factor，而是对奇异值施加一个平滑函数。论文把这一有限迭代表示为一个 smoothed spectral potential 的梯度，即 update direction = grad Phi_q(M)，其中 Phi_q 作用在奇异值上。这样 Muon update 可以被看成 gradient-based prediction algorithm。regret 分解为两项：penalty term 衡量平滑势函数和 nuclear norm 的距离，q 越大越小；stability term 由诱导映射的 Lipschitz 常数控制，q 越大通常越大。选择 q = O(log(1/epsilon)) 可以平衡两项，让有限 Newton–Schulz 足够接近 polar，又保持可控平滑性。这个分析和把有限迭代当 approximation error 的思路不同：它不是证明“有限步足够像 exact polar”，而是利用“有限步不像 exact polar 的地方”来获得稳定性。
summary.experiments: 论文主要是理论结果，不以大规模预训练实验为核心。设目标函数 Lipschitz、可非光滑且非凸；随机梯度 oracle 无偏且噪声有界。对任意半径 rho > 0 和精度 epsilon > 0，带 momentum 且每轮使用 q = O(log(1/epsilon)) 步 Newton–Schulz 的 Muon，可以在期望意义下用 O(rho^{-1} epsilon^{-3} + epsilon^{-2}) 次随机梯度调用找到一个 (rho, epsilon)-stationary point。stationarity 采用 Jiang et al. 2026a 的定义。主导项 rho^{-1} epsilon^{-3} 与 Pion、Leon 在相同 stationarity 标准下的保证相匹配，但算法更接近真实 Muon，因为它没有引入额外的随机扰动或 momentum augmentation。论文还对比了 exact-polar Muon 的失败模式：exact polar 对应的 online learner 可能有线性 regret，因此不能通过该框架得到收敛到 stationary point 的保证。
summary.reading_guide: 建议精读。先看 Introduction，重点是三条线索：Muon 在 LLM 预训练中的工程动机、exact polar 理论的问题、finite Newton–Schulz 为什么可能带来平滑性。Section 2 要看清楚作者分析的 Muon 变体和真实部署 Muon 的差异，包括 momentum、随机梯度假设、Newton–Schulz 深度和矩阵参数设定。核心创新应在把有限 Newton–Schulz 写成 smoothed spectral potential 的梯度，以及由此得到 discounted regret bound 的部分；这部分决定了论文的技术价值。定理部分重点看 q 与 epsilon 的关系、penalty/stability trade-off，以及 O2NC 如何把 regret 转成 (rho, epsilon)-stationarity。Appendix A 适合用来和 Pion、Leon 的复杂度做对照。Section 6 若存在部署差异讨论，适合判断该理论离真实 LLM pretraining recipe 还有哪些距离，例如 weight decay、per-layer scaling、混合精度数值误差、矩形矩阵处理和实际 Newton–Schulz 系数选择。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper addresses a gap in the theory of Muon. Practical Muon uses a finite number of Newton–Schulz iterations to approximately orthogonalize matrix-valued momentum, but existing analyses either replace this loop with the exact polar factor or treat finite depth as approximation error. The paper shows that, for nonsmooth nonconvex optimization, finite Newton–Schulz can be the mechanism that enables convergence.
summary_en.importance: This is directly relevant to LLM pretraining optimization. Muon is attractive because most LLM parameters are matrices and its matrix-momentum orthogonalization can improve update geometry at scale. The theoretical issue is that the exact polar map is discontinuous and, under the online-learning view, exact-polar Muon behaves like follow-the-leader over the operator-norm ball, which can incur linear regret. The paper explains why the implementation detail used in practice—truncating Newton–Schulz after a few matrix-multiply steps—can improve the optimization theory by smoothing the polar map. The contribution is not a new pretraining recipe; it is a sharper explanation of why the practical optimizer may have better stability properties than its exact-polar idealization.
summary_en.technical_approach: The analysis uses the online-to-nonconvex conversion framework. The optimizer’s update rule is treated as an online learner, and the learner’s regret is converted into a Goldstein-style stationarity guarantee for nonsmooth nonconvex objectives. For a momentum matrix M = U Sigma V^T, the ideal Muon direction is the polar factor U V^T, which preserves singular subspaces and maps all positive singular values to one. This hard singular-value map is discontinuous. Finite Newton–Schulz replaces it with a polynomial map obtained by q iterations of an odd matrix polynomial, implemented with matrix multiplications rather than an SVD. The paper shows that this finite-depth map is the gradient of a smoothed spectral potential evaluated at the momentum matrix. This turns Muon into a gradient-based prediction algorithm. The discounted regret decomposes into a penalty term and a stability term. The penalty decreases as the smoothed potential approaches the nuclear norm; the stability term is controlled by the Lipschitz constant of the finite Newton–Schulz map. Choosing q = O(log(1/epsilon)) balances these terms. The key conceptual move is to use the finite-depth deviation from the exact polar factor as smoothing, rather than treating it only as approximation error.
summary_en.experiments: The paper is primarily theoretical. Under a Lipschitz objective that may be nonsmooth and nonconvex, with an unbiased stochastic gradient oracle and bounded noise, Muon with momentum and q = O(log(1/epsilon)) Newton–Schulz steps per round finds a (rho, epsilon)-stationary point in expectation using O(rho^{-1} epsilon^{-3} + epsilon^{-2}) stochastic gradient evaluations. The stationarity notion follows Jiang et al. 2026a. The leading rho^{-1} epsilon^{-3} term matches the guarantees reported for Pion and Leon under the same criterion, while staying closer to the Muon update used in practice because it does not add stochastic perturbations or augment the momentum matrix. The paper also contrasts this with exact-polar Muon, which can fail to converge in the same framework because its corresponding online learner can suffer linear regret.
summary_en.reading_guide: Read carefully. The introduction is useful for understanding why exact-polar analyses miss an important feature of practical Muon. Section 2 should be checked for the exact Muon variant being analyzed and for the assumptions on stochastic gradients, momentum, matrix parameters, and Newton–Schulz depth. The main technical sections to focus on are the representation of finite Newton–Schulz as the gradient of a smoothed spectral potential and the discounted-regret proof. The most important details are the penalty-versus-stability trade-off, the logarithmic dependence q = O(log(1/epsilon)), and how the online-to-nonconvex conversion yields the final stationarity complexity. Appendix A is useful for comparing the rate with Pion and Leon. Any discussion of remaining differences from deployed Muon is worth reading to assess how the theory maps to real LLM pretraining, including weight decay, layerwise scaling, numerical precision, rectangular matrices, and the exact Newton–Schulz coefficients used in practice.

recommendation.zh: 应读；它把 Muon 的有限 NS 从“近似误差”改成“有用平滑”，值得进内部 optimizer ablation 的解释框架。
recommendation.en: Read it; it reframes Muon’s finite NS steps from approximation error to useful smoothing, a better lens for internal optimizer ablations.

paper.abstract: Orthogonal optimisers such as Muon can substantially accelerate large language model pretraining relative to Adam, yet the mechanism remains incompletely understood.
