summary.core_problem: 现有自适应优化器的逐坐标预条件不满足深度网络参数连续对称性的等变要求，会导致优化轨迹偏离对称商空间，改变收敛极小点并模糊奇异学习率的可测量性。
summary.importance: 揭示了主流自适应优化器在处理架构对称性时的根本缺陷，解释了部分训练不稳定、过拟合、泛化差异的优化层面原因；提出的DDC框架可与任意基础优化器结合，为LLM预训练优化器设计提供了新的等变约束思路；在grokking、语言模型过训练、ViT训练等场景的验证结果对优化LLM训练recipe、提升收敛质量有直接参考价值。
summary.technical_approach: 构建死方向预条件器（DDC），将基础优化器提升为G等变优化器：在G不变度量的轨道分解下拆分预条件状态，水平方向（商空间有效维度）保留等变的逐坐标自适应，垂直方向（对称轨道/死方向）将每个轨道维度的预条件压缩为单个标量，避免轨迹漂移到死方向；覆盖四类架构规范，三类阿贝尔规范（交叉熵平移、ReLU/SwiGLU缩放、LayerNorm/RMSNorm缩放）用逐通道标量二阶矩即可精确等变，非阿贝尔的注意力头旋转规范提供从单标量到体坐标系topk自适应的多种实现；实例化DDCAdam与DDCMuon，理论证明其在商空间上执行预条件梯度流且离散步偏差有界。
summary.experiments: 12层语言模型过训练场景下，DDCAdam避免了AdamW的过训练崩溃，且能读出AdamW无法测量的奇异收敛速率；从零训练的ViT上，DDCAdam达到更低验证损失，且在权重衰减下能压缩冗余前馈容量，而AdamW保留冗余参数；grokking Transformer上，DDC将规范模式量级压到比AdamW低数个数量级，DDCMuon在24层深度下11个种子中有10个出现grokking，普通Muon无一个成功，且收敛到退化程度更低的极小点；环面规范与旋转位置编码几何匹配后，相同权重衰减下grokking速度更快。
summary.reading_guide: 重点阅读第1章引言中对称性导致优化器漂移的推导、DDC轨道分解预条件的核心设计、四类架构规范的具体处理方案、grokking与语言模型过训练的实验结果；预计阅读时间35-40分钟，无需深究奇异学习率定理的数学证明，重点把握优化器设计思路与实验结论。

summary_en.core_problem: Per-coordinate preconditioning in existing adaptive optimizers fails to satisfy the equivariance requirement of deep networks' continuous parameter symmetries, causing optimization trajectories to drift off the symmetry quotient space, altering converged minima, and blurring the measurability of singular learning rates.
summary_en.importance: Reveals a fundamental flaw of mainstream adaptive optimizers in handling architectural symmetries, explaining optimization-level causes of training instability, overfitting, and generalization gaps in some scenarios; the proposed DDC framework is compatible with arbitrary base optimizers, providing a new equivariance-constrained approach for LLM pretraining optimizer design; validations on grokking, language model overtraining, and ViT training offer direct references for optimizing LLM training recipes and improving convergence quality.
summary_en.technical_approach: Builds the Dead-Direction Conditioner (DDC) that lifts a base optimizer into a G-equivariant one: it splits the preconditioning state under the orbit decomposition of a G-invariant metric, retaining equivariant per-coordinate adaptivity for the horizontal component (effective quotient space dimensions) and collapsing the preconditioner for each vertical (symmetry orbit / dead direction) dimension into a single scalar to prevent trajectory drift. It covers four architectural gauges: three abelian gauges (cross-entropy shift, ReLU/SwiGLU rescaling, LayerNorm/RMSNorm scaling) achieve exact equivariance with per-channel scalar second moments, while the non-abelian per-head attention rotation gauge offers a spectrum of implementations from a single scalar per head to top-k adaptivity in the body frame (eigenbasis of W^T W). Two instantiations, DDCAdam and DDCMuon, are provided with theoretical proof that they execute preconditioned gradient flow on the quotient space with bounded discrete-step bias.
summary_en.experiments: In the overtraining regime of a 12-layer language model, DDCAdam avoids the overtraining collapse observed in AdamW and reads the singular convergence rate that AdamW fails to measure; on a ViT trained from scratch, DDCAdam achieves lower validation loss and compresses redundant feed-forward capacity under weight decay while AdamW leaves redundant parameters intact; on the grokking Transformer, DDC suppresses gauge mode magnitudes by orders of magnitude compared to AdamW, DDCMuon achieves grokking in 10 out of 11 random seeds at 24-layer depth while plain Muon achieves none, and converges to a less degenerate minimum; matching a torus gauge to rotary position encoding geometry accelerates grokking at the same weight decay level.
summary_en.reading_guide: Focus on Section 1 (derivation of optimizer drift caused by architectural symmetries), core design of DDC's orbit-decomposed preconditioning, specific handling schemes for four architectural gauges, and experimental results on grokking and language model overtraining; estimated reading time 35-40 minutes, no need to dive into the mathematical proof of the singular learning rate theorem, prioritize understanding the optimizer design logic and empirical conclusions.

recommendation.zh: 先看理论 setup 和 Adam/Muon 组合部分；若实验足够干净，这类 gauge 修正值得放进内部 optimizer ablation。
recommendation.en: Read the theoretical setup and the Adam/Muon composition first; if the experiments are clean, this gauge-aware fix deserves an internal optimizer ablation.

paper.title: Muon learns balanced solutions in matrix factorization without slow saddle-to-saddle dynamics
paper.abstract: Matrix factorization (i.e., problems of the form $\min_{\mathbf{P},\mathbf{Q}} \|\mathbf{M}^\star - \mathbf{P}^\top\mathbf{Q}\|_\mathrm{F}^2$) is a minimal learning problem that exhibits both nonlinear parameter dynamics and representation learning. In this setting, we study how parameter trajectories under the Muon optimizer differ from those of gradient descent. We identify three main dynamical differences: 1) Muon avoids the slow saddle-to-saddle dynamics from small initialization. Muon inste

summary.core_problem: 这篇论文用矩阵分解作为最小模型，分析 Muon optimizer 的正交化更新为什么会产生不同于梯度下降的学习动力学。
summary.importance: 它对预训练的价值不在直接给出大模型 recipe，而在解释 Muon 类优化器可能为何适合大模型训练。论文指出，Muon 的更新不继承梯度奇异值谱，而是把梯度方向极分解成半正交矩阵后再更新。这会改变模式学习顺序、学习率稳定区间和解的平衡性。对大模型训练里的 Muon、正交化梯度、学习率 annealing/cooldown 设计都有参考意义。
summary.technical_approach: 论文研究无 momentum 版本的 Muon：对权重矩阵 W，先对梯度 G 做 polar orthogonalization，得到 U V^T，再用 eta 乘这个半正交方向更新。对比普通梯度下降，GD 的更新直接继承梯度谱，Muon 的每个矩阵更新则有统一的奇异值尺度。分析对象是矩阵分解 L(P,Q)=1/2 ||M* - P Q^T||^2，P 和 Q 从小的各向同性高斯初始化开始。作者把学习过程拆成几个阶段：早期 P 与 Q 的右奇异向量先相互对齐，随后模型 P Q^T 的奇异向量与目标 M* 对齐；对齐后，权重奇异值近似均匀增长，模型奇异值到达目标值附近后进入振荡；若要严格收敛，需要学习率退火。论文还构造了一个三阶段学习率日程：小步先让 P/Q 对齐，大步把模型推到目标解流形附近，最后通过退火收敛。
summary.experiments: 实验主要服务于理论验证，而不是大规模神经网络训练。作者用矩阵分解数值实验对比 Muon 与梯度下降：GD 从小初始化出发会出现 slow saddle-to-saddle dynamics，模式按奇异值大小逐步学习，并且学习率受局部 sharpness 阈值限制；Muon 倾向于同时学习目标的 top modes，小模式可更早到达目标附近，并且在超过 GD 稳定阈值的学习率下仍能保持稳定但会振荡。文段没有给出具体维度、曲线数值或误差表，因此这里只能概括实验结论。
summary.reading_guide: 建议泛读，预计 30 到 45 分钟。重点看 Introduction 的三条动力学差异、Section 3 的 post-alignment 分析、Section 4 的奇异向量对齐速率，以及 Section 5 的三阶段学习率构造。对做大模型预训练的人，最有用的是两个点：一是 Muon 为什么减弱梯度谱条件数对更新速度的约束；二是为什么即使 Muon 能快速到达解附近，仍然需要 annealing 才能消除振荡并稳定收敛。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper analyzes how Muon’s orthogonalized matrix updates change learning dynamics in matrix factorization, using it as a minimal setting with nonlinear parameters and representation learning.
summary_en.importance: The paper is useful for pretraining research as an optimizer-dynamics study. It does not provide a direct large-model training recipe, but it clarifies why Muon-style updates can behave differently from gradient descent: the update direction is spectrally normalized through polar orthogonalization, so the optimizer is less tied to the singular-value profile of the raw gradient. This has implications for learning-rate choice, annealing, and the role of balanced matrix representations in large models.
summary_en.technical_approach: The studied Muon rule is momentum-free. For a weight matrix W and gradient G, the update uses the matrix sign or polar factor of G: if G = U S V^T, the update direction is U V^T. The optimization problem is L(P,Q)=1/2 ||M* - P Q^T||^2 with small isotropic Gaussian initialization. The analysis describes a staged trajectory. First, the right singular subspaces of P and Q align with each other, and the model singular vectors align with those of the target matrix. After alignment, the singular values of P and Q grow nearly uniformly; model modes saturate once they reach the target singular values and then oscillate around the solution unless the learning rate is annealed. The paper also constructs a three-stage schedule: a small initial step for P/Q alignment, a large step to align the model with the target and move it near the solution manifold, and a final annealing phase for convergence.
summary_en.experiments: The empirical component is mainly numerical validation of the derived dynamics in matrix factorization. The reported qualitative differences are clear: gradient descent from small initialization exhibits slow saddle-to-saddle behavior and sequential mode learning, while Muon learns the leading target modes at comparable rates, with smaller modes often reaching their targets first. Muon also remains stable beyond learning-rate thresholds that would be problematic for gradient descent under local sharpness. The provided text does not include exact dimensions, error values, or curve statistics, so the results should be read as mechanistic evidence rather than a quantitative large-scale optimizer benchmark.
summary_en.reading_guide: Skim in about 30 to 45 minutes. Read the introduction for the three main dynamical claims, Section 3 for the post-alignment regime and the need for annealing, Section 4 for singular-vector alignment rates, and Section 5 for the constructed learning-rate schedule. For foundation-model training, the most relevant question is how orthogonalized updates decouple progress from gradient spectra, and why annealing or cooldown remains important even when the optimizer reaches the solution neighborhood quickly.

recommendation.zh: 从矩阵分解的视角理论分析了最近很火的 Muon 优化器，解释了它为什么能摆脱 condition number 限制并允许极大学习率，对理解和改进预训练优化器很有帮助。
recommendation.en: Theoretically analyzes the trending Muon optimizer from a matrix factorization perspective, explaining why it escapes condition number limits and allows huge learning rates. Very helpful for understanding and improving pre-training optimizers.

paper.title: Aurora: A Leverage-Aware Spectral Optimizer
paper.abstract: We show that for tall matrix parameters, like projection matrices in the MLP layers, the Muon update can have row norms that are arbitrarily non-uniform. This can lead to a self-reinforcing feedback loop whereby neurons receive persistently small updates and eventually do not contribute meaningfully to network outputs. This problem is effectively mitigated by an additional row normalization step, but current methods do this in a way that moves the Muon update geometry away from the polar factor

summary.core_problem: 解决Muon等谱优化器在高瘦矩阵参数上更新行范数不均，导致部分MLP神经元长期更新不足的问题。
summary.importance: 贡献类型是预训练优化器改进和训练动态诊断；它把一个看似细节的矩阵更新几何问题连接到神经元失活和MLP扩张比例，是值得复现实验的训练侧信号。
summary.technical_approach: 论文先指出Muon对高瘦矩阵的polar-factor更新可能产生任意不均匀的row norm，并形成自增强反馈：更新小的神经元继续变弱。Aurora在保持Muon动量矩阵极分解几何的同时，对矩阵参数更新施加行均匀性约束，避免已有row normalization破坏polar-factor几何。
summary.experiments: 摘要称Aurora在预训练实验中优于Muon；与现有方法结合后，在modded-nanoGPT speedrun的optimizer track中达到谱优化器中的最佳表现。还观察到Aurora相对Muon的收益会随MLP expansion factor增大而变强；摘要未给出模型规模和具体loss/token效率数字。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper addresses non-uniform row norms in Muon-style spectral optimizer updates for tall matrix parameters, which can leave some MLP neurons persistently under-updated.
summary_en.importance: The contribution is a pretraining optimizer and training-dynamics result. It connects matrix-update geometry to neuron under-training and MLP expansion, making it a useful signal for internal optimizer ablations.
summary_en.technical_approach: The paper argues that Muon's polar-factor update can have arbitrarily non-uniform row norms on tall matrices, creating a feedback loop where weakly updated neurons contribute less. Aurora enforces row-uniform matrix updates while preserving the polar-factor geometry of the momentum matrix, unlike simpler row-normalization fixes.
summary_en.experiments: The abstract reports that Aurora outperforms Muon in pretraining experiments and, when combined with existing methods, achieves the best spectral-optimizer result on the optimizer track of the modded-nanoGPT speedrun. It also finds that Aurora's gains over Muon grow with the MLP expansion factor, but does not give exact model sizes or loss numbers.

recommendation.zh: 应在小规模internal pretrain立刻复现；若行范数反馈成立，Muon系优化器在大MLP上要重新调prior。
recommendation.en: Reproduce this in a small internal pretrain; if the row-norm feedback holds, Muon-style optimizers need a new prior for wide MLPs.

paper.title: DMuon: Efficient Distributed Muon Training with Near-Adam Overhead
paper.abstract: Matrix-orthogonalization-based optimizers, exemplified by Muon, have demonstrated strong convergence behavior across a wide range of modern deep learning workloads. The matrix-aware updates offer a compelling alternative to conventional element-wise optimization, particularly as model architectures continue to grow in scale and heterogeneity. Yet contemporary distributed training infrastructure built around the assumption of element-wise optimizers is poorly matched to matrix-level optimizers su

summary.core_problem: 矩阵正交化优化器 Muon 在收敛效率上相比 AdamW 有显著优势，但其 Newton-Schulz 迭代作用于完整权重矩阵，与当前基于逐元素优化假设构建的分布式训练栈（参数按 shard 分置于各 rank）存在结构性失配。每一步需要重建完整矩阵带来的额外通信与计算开销，使原生 Muon 实现的 optimizer step 耗时超过前向+反向的总和，抵消了其 FLOP 级收敛优势，阻碍了大规模训练中的实际部署。
summary.importance: 首次系统解决分布式场景下矩阵感知优化器的系统开销问题，将 Muon 的实际 step 开销压缩到接近 AdamW 的水平，使 Muon 的收敛收益能真正转化为 wall-clock 端到端训练加速。方案已在 WALL-OSS-0.5、WALL-WM 等生产级任务中验证，对预训练优化器栈的下一代演进（从逐元素到矩阵感知）有直接的工程落地价值，也为 FSDP/ZeRO 与非逐元素优化器的兼容设计提供了明确方向。
summary.technical_approach: DMuon 是一个可即插即用的分布式 Muon 模块，与宿主训练框架、并行策略解耦，核心设计分四层：1) owner-centric 通信优化：为每个完整矩阵选定一个 owner rank，非 owner 把各自 shard 通过一次 all-gather 聚合到 owner，在 owner 上执行完整 Newton-Schulz 迭代后再把更新后的 shard 分发回去，通信量最小且保留精确优化器语义；避免了逐 shard 计算无法正交化的根本问题。2) 形状自适应执行栈：采用批量 Gram Newton-Schulz 执行（先算 M M^T / M^T M 再迭代，减少运算量）、对称感知专用 kernel（利用 Gram 矩阵对称减半计算）、DSL 驱动的自动调优，在异构形状的大量矩阵上都能达到高算力利用率。3) 计算感知负载均衡：将 owner 分配建模为基于实测耗时的优化问题，结合 batching、kernel 选择、自动调优带来的非线性开销，在运行时 profile 后做全局分配，避免 owner 之间负载不均。4) 即插即用接口：对现有训练管线只暴露标准优化器调用，底层兼容 ZeRO、FSDP2、张量并行等多种切分方式，不改训练主循环。与原生 Muon 相比，DMuon 不做任何算法近似，保持完全相同的更新规则与收敛行为。
summary.experiments: 在三类任务上验证：1) 机器人 VLA 训练（WALL-OSS-0.5、WALL-WM）：VLA 任务前向反向计算占比低，optimizer 开销问题最突出。DMuon 实现了接近 AdamW 的 optimizer step 开销（差距通常在 10%–20% 以内），而原生 Muon 是 AdamW 的 2 倍以上；端到端 step 时间相比原生 Muon 显著降低，同时完整保留 Muon 的收敛曲线与最终性能。2) 语言模型预训练：不同参数规模、张量并行宽度下，DMuon 的额外开销相比 AdamW 控制在小范围，在大模型宽并行设置下通信优化的收益更明显。3) 消融实验逐项验证 owner 选择策略、批量 Gram 执行、对称 kernel、自动调优各自的贡献，其中 owner-centric 通信与批量 Gram Newton-Schulz 是两项最大的单点收益来源。论文给出的核心结论是，Muon 在 FLOP 层面的收敛优势可以通过 DMuon 无损耗地转化为 wall-clock 层面的实际训练加速。
summary.reading_guide: 精读。先看 §2 背景部分，彻底理清 Muon 的 Newton-Schulz 迭代输入是完整矩阵这一特性，以及它与 ZeRO / FSDP / TP 三种切分方式分别冲突在哪里——这是整篇论文设计的根因。再读 §3 四层技术方案：重点读图 2 的 owner-centric 数据流，理解为什么选 owner + all-gather 比跨 rank 协同做 Newton-Schulz 更简洁高效；§3.2 的 Gram Newton-Schulz 推导与对称 kernel 是性能翻倍的关键；§3.3 的负载均衡建模思路有通用参考价值。§4 实验部分重点看不同任务下 optimizer step 时间、端到端 step 时间相对于 AdamW 和原生 Muon 的柱状对比，以及参数规模/并行宽度对开销的影响曲线。附录里的 kernel 细节与自动调优 DSL 对工程实现有直接价值。值得深挖的点：这套框架对其他矩阵感知优化器（如 Shampoo、SOAP 变体）的可迁移性，以及 MoE 场景下大量专家矩阵的 owner 分配策略。
summary.authors_note: WALL 团队与伯克利相关作者（含 Moonlight、WALL-OSS 系列工作的主要作者群），涉及机器人基础模型与大规模训练系统方向。

summary_en.core_problem: Matrix-orthogonalizing optimizers like Muon provide clear convergence advantages over AdamW, but their Newton-Schulz iteration requires operating on full weight matrices. This is fundamentally mismatched with modern distributed training stacks built around the element-wise optimizer assumption, where parameters are split into shards across ranks. Reconstructing full matrices at every optimizer step introduces heavy communication and computation overhead: naive Muon implementations often spend more time in the optimizer step than in the combined forward and backward passes, erasing Muon's FLOP-level convergence advantage and blocking its large-scale deployment.
summary_en.importance: Presents the first systematic solution to the systems overhead of matrix-aware optimizers in distributed settings, compressing Muon's real step overhead to a level close to AdamW. As a result, Muon's convergence gains translate directly into wall-clock end-to-end training speedups. Validated in production-grade workloads including WALL-OSS-0.5 and WALL-WM, the work has immediate engineering value for the next-generation optimizer stack (element-wise to matrix-aware) and provides a clear template for making FSDP / ZeRO compatible with non-element-wise update rules.
summary_en.technical_approach: DMuon is a drop-in distributed Muon module orthogonal to the host training framework and parallelism strategy. Its design has four layers. (1) Owner-centric communication optimization: one owner rank is selected per full matrix. Non-owners aggregate their shards to the owner via a single all-gather, the full Newton-Schulz iteration runs on the owner, and updated shards are then scattered back. Communication volume is minimized while exact optimizer semantics are preserved, addressing the root issue that per-shard computation cannot perform orthogonalization. (2) Shape-adaptive execution stack: combines batched Gram Newton-Schulz execution (computing MM^T / M^TM first then iterating, reducing arithmetic), symmetry-aware specialized kernels (halving work on symmetric Gram matrices), and DSL-driven autotuning to deliver high utilization across heterogeneous matrix shapes. (3) Computation-aware load balancing: owner assignment is formulated as a measured-cost optimization problem. A runtime profile captures the nonlinear costs introduced by batching, kernel selection, and autotuning, then performs global assignment to balance work across owners. (4) Drop-in interface: exposes only a standard optimizer API to existing pipelines, natively supports ZeRO, FSDP2, and tensor parallel sharding without modifying the main training loop. DMuon performs no algorithmic approximation; update rules and convergence behavior are identical to naive Muon.
summary_en.experiments: Validated across three classes of workloads. (1) Robotics VLA training (WALL-OSS-0.5, WALL-WM): VLA tasks have low forward/backward compute density, so optimizer overhead is most severe. DMuon reaches near-AdamW optimizer step cost (typically within 10%–20%), while naive Muon exceeds 2x AdamW cost. End-to-end step time is significantly reduced against naive Muon, with Muon's convergence curve and final quality fully preserved. (2) Language model pretraining: across parameter scales and tensor-parallel widths, DMuon's additional overhead over AdamW stays in a small range, with larger gains in large-model wide-parallel configurations where communication optimization matters most. (3) Ablations quantify the contribution of each component: owner-centric communication and batched Gram Newton-Schulz are the two largest single-point gains. The core result is that Muon's FLOP-level convergence advantage is converted, without loss, into actual wall-clock training speedup via DMuon.
summary_en.reading_guide: Close read. Start with §2 Background to build a solid understanding of two facts: that Muon's Newton-Schulz iteration operates on full matrices, and exactly how this conflicts with ZeRO / FSDP2 / tensor parallel sharding — this is the root motivation for the entire design. Then work through §3's four technical layers, focusing on: the owner-centric data flow in Figure 2 and why owner + all-gather is simpler and more efficient than cross-rank cooperative Newton-Schulz; the Gram Newton-Schulz derivation and symmetry kernels in §3.2 which drive the largest compute reductions; the load-balancing formulation in §3.3, which has generalizable value. In §4 Experiments, track the bar charts of optimizer-step time and end-to-end step time against AdamW / naive Muon across tasks, and the scaling curves of overhead vs. parameter count / parallelism width. Appendix details on kernel implementations and the autotuning DSL are of direct value for engineering deployment. Worth further investigation: portability of this framework to other matrix-aware optimizers (Shampoo, SOAP variants), and owner assignment strategies for the large expert-matrix populations in MoE setups.
summary_en.authors_note: WALL team together with Berkeley-affiliated authors, including the main contributors to the Moonlight and WALL-OSS series, working on robotics foundation models and large-scale training systems.

recommendation.zh: 应立刻看实现细节并复现实验；Muon 的瓶颈若真被系统化解，优化器 ablation 的成本结构会变。
recommendation.en: Read the implementation details and reproduce it; if Muon’s overhead is really systemically removed, optimizer ablation economics change.

paper.title: Hierarchical Muon: Tiled Newton-Schulz Updates for Efficient Muon Optimization
paper.abstract: Muon-type optimizers construct update directions for dense neural-network weights by applying a finite Newton-Schulz map to momentum-gradient matrices. For an $H \times W$ matrix, with $r=\min\{H,W\}$ and $s=\max\{H,W\}$, $K$ steps of the full-matrix Newton-Schulz update require $O(r^2 s K)$ work and couple all rows and columns through repeated Gram matrix products. We introduce Hierarchical Muon (HiMuon), a tiled Newton-Schulz scheme for Muon-type optimization. HiMuon partitions each momentum-g

summary.core_problem: 标准Muon优化器的全矩阵Newton-Schulz更新计算复杂度高（O(r²sK)），存在全局谱耦合，分布式参数分片训练下还需要额外集合通信重构完整矩阵，制约了大模型预训练阶段的优化器执行效率。
summary.importance: 为预训练优化器设计提供了谱耦合范围与计算开销可显式权衡的新思路，HiMuon的分块实现可直接降低Transformer预训练的优化器时延，且原生适配分布式参数分片布局，对大模型训练系统优化有实际工程参考价值。
summary.technical_approach: 提出分层Muon（HiMuon），将每个动量-梯度矩阵划分为T×T的分块网格，对每个分块独立执行K步Newton-Schulz迭代后重组输出。分块大小T同时作为数值参数（控制保留的谱耦合范围）和计算参数（控制Newton-Schulz迭代开销）。实现层面针对分块后的批量小矩阵运算做了定制化kernel、跨层批处理、内存受限分块、运行时分块大小调度，且支持分布式场景下各rank本地完成分块计算，无需额外跨分片通信。
summary.experiments: 在矩阵函数层、单层级别、优化器步级别、端到端训练四个层级完成评估，覆盖Transformer真实权重形状、kernel与分块形状选型、跨层批处理收益、有限精度下Newton-Schulz计算与训练质量的权衡，还引入关联记忆基准作为分块大小选择的结构诊断工具。核心结论是当T远小于矩阵最小维度时，Newton-Schulz计算的主导复杂度大幅下降，且可在训练质量与速度间取得平滑的可调权衡。
summary.reading_guide: 重点关注第4章HiMuon算法与GPU实现细节、第6章的效率与训练质量消融实验。预计阅读时间15-20分钟，若已熟悉Muon优化器基础可跳过第2章预备知识部分。

summary_en.core_problem: The full-matrix Newton-Schulz (NS) update in standard Muon optimizers has high computational complexity (O(r²sK)), introduces global spectral coupling across all matrix entries, and requires extra collective communication to reconstruct full matrices in distributed parameter-sharded training, limiting optimizer throughput during large-scale LLM pretraining.
summary_en.importance: Introduces an explicit, tunable tradeoff between spectral coupling scope and computational cost for pretraining optimizers. HiMuon's tiled implementation directly reduces optimizer latency in Transformer pretraining and natively supports distributed parameter-sharded layouts, delivering practical engineering insights for large-scale training system optimization.
summary_en.technical_approach: Proposes Hierarchical Muon (HiMuon), which partitions each momentum-gradient matrix into a T×T tile grid, applies K-step NS iterations independently to each tile, then reassembles the outputs. Tile size T acts as both a numerical hyperparameter (controlling the retained spectral coupling range) and a computational parameter (controlling NS iteration cost). The implementation includes tile-size-specific kernels, cross-layer batching, memory-bounded chunking, runtime tile-size scheduling, and support for local per-rank tiled computation in distributed settings without cross-shard communication overhead.
summary_en.experiments: Evaluations are conducted at four levels: matrix-function, per-layer, optimizer-step, and end-to-end training. Experiments cover real Transformer weight shapes, kernel/tile shape selection, cross-layer batching gains, finite-precision NS computation tradeoffs with training quality, plus an associative-memory benchmark as a structural diagnostic for tile size selection. The key finding is that when T is far smaller than the minimum matrix dimension, the leading-order NS computation cost drops significantly, with a smooth, tunable tradeoff between training quality and throughput.
summary_en.reading_guide: Focus on Section 4 (HiMuon algorithm and GPU implementation details) and Section 6 (ablation studies on efficiency and training quality). Estimated reading time: 15-20 minutes; skip Section 2 preliminaries if already familiar with standard Muon optimizer fundamentals.

recommendation.zh: 读算法和 tile-size ablation 就够；它的关键不是近似 full Muon，而是定义了另一个局部谱优化器。
recommendation.en: Read the algorithm and tile-size ablations; the key is not approximating full Muon, but defining a different local spectral optimizer.

paper.title: Muown Implicitly Performs Angular Step-size Decay
paper.abstract: Matrix-aware optimizers such as Muon and Muown have recently shown strong empirical performance for pre-training Transformers. In particular, Muown separates each weight matrix into row magnitudes and an un-normalized direction variable, updating the former with Adam and the latter with Muon. We show that the directional update of Muown is equivalent to a Riemannian step on the normalized directions, while the magnitude of the un-normalized parameterization only modulates the angular step size.

summary.core_problem: Muown 优化器在 Transformer 预训练中表现出极强的步长稳定性，但其背后的机制尚不明确。本文旨在揭示 Muown 稳定性的几何本质，并基于此提出一种更显式、更易调参的改进算法。
summary.importance: 本文不仅从黎曼流形的角度解释了 Muown 的成功机制，还提出了一种新的优化器 AngularMuown。该优化器将角度步长作为显式可调参数，在多个规模的 Transformer 预训练中展现出比 AdamW 和 Muown 更快的收敛速度，为大模型预训练优化器设计提供了新的思路。
summary.technical_approach: 作者首先证明了 Muown 对权重矩阵方向的更新等价于在行倾斜流形（row-oblique manifold）上的黎曼更新。在这个视角下，Muown 的方向更新步长与行范数成反比。随着训练进行，行范数增长，导致角度步长隐式衰减，这解释了 Muown 的步长稳定性。基于此，作者提出了 AngularMuown：显式地保持方向矩阵归一化，并在其上执行黎曼 Muon 更新。关键在于，AngularMuown 将角度步长与径向幅度更新解耦，使其成为一个可独立调度的显式参数。
summary.experiments: 在 124M、500M 稠密模型以及 1.1B MoE 模型的预训练实验中，AngularMuown 持续优于 AdamW、Muon 和 Muown。特别是在收敛速度上，AngularMuown 展现出显著优势。此外，作者还提供了非凸设定下的理论收敛性证明。
summary.reading_guide: 建议重点阅读 Section 2 中关于 Muown 隐式黎曼更新的几何解释，以及 Section 3 中 AngularMuown 的算法推导。Section 4 的实验结果展示了其在不同规模模型上的有效性。值得深挖的是角度步长调度策略对训练动态的具体影响。

summary_en.core_problem: The Muown optimizer exhibits remarkable step-size stability in Transformer pre-training, but the underlying mechanism remains unclear. This paper aims to uncover the geometric nature of Muown's stability and propose an improved algorithm that is more explicit and easier to tune.
summary_en.importance: This paper not only explains the success mechanism of Muown from the perspective of Riemannian manifolds but also proposes a new optimizer, AngularMuown. By making the angular step size an explicit, tunable parameter, AngularMuown demonstrates faster convergence than AdamW and Muown in Transformer pre-training across various scales, offering new insights for optimizer design in large model pre-training.
summary_en.technical_approach: The authors first prove that Muown's directional update on weight matrices is equivalent to a Riemannian update on the row-oblique manifold. In this view, the directional update step size is inversely proportional to the row norm. As the row norm grows during training, the angular step size implicitly decays, explaining Muown's step-size stability. Building on this, the authors propose AngularMuown: explicitly keeping the direction matrix normalized and performing Riemannian Muon updates on it. Crucially, AngularMuown decouples the angular step size from the radial magnitude update, making it an independent, schedulable explicit parameter.
summary_en.experiments: In pre-training experiments on 124M and 500M dense models, as well as a 1.1B MoE model, AngularMuown consistently outperforms AdamW, Muon, and Muown. It shows a significant advantage in convergence speed. Additionally, the authors provide a theoretical convergence proof in the non-convex setting.
summary_en.reading_guide: It is recommended to focus on the geometric explanation of Muown's implicit Riemannian update in Section 2, and the algorithm derivation of AngularMuown in Section 3. The experimental results in Section 4 demonstrate its effectiveness across different model scales. A point worth exploring further is the specific impact of the angular step-size scheduling strategy on training dynamics.

recommendation.zh: 应读证明和 Qwen ablation；它把 Muown 的黑盒收益压成角步长控制，值得立刻小规模复现。
recommendation.en: Read the proof and Qwen ablations; it reduces Muown’s opaque gain to angular step-size control and is worth reproducing at small scale.

paper.title: Towards Understanding the Power and Limits of the Muon Optimizer: A River-Valley Perspective
paper.abstract: Recently, Muon has gained substantial attention as an appealing alternative to Adam-like optimizers, with many works highlighting its advantages through spectral normalization and improved conditioning. Yet this positive theoretical narrative contrasts with its empirical performance in large language model (LLM) training, where Muon's gains over Adam/AdamW are often mixed, schedule-sensitive, and not uniformly superior. To address this gap, we develop a trajectory-level theory characterizing bot

summary.core_problem: 这篇论文研究 Muon 优化器为什么在 LLM 训练中有时有效、有时不稳定。现有解释通常强调 Muon 通过梯度正交化改善谱条件数，能更均匀地利用低能量奇异方向；但大模型训练中的实证表现并不总是优于 AdamW，且对学习率 schedule 和训练阶段敏感。作者要回答的问题是：Muon 的优势和限制分别来自优化轨迹中的哪一部分。
summary.importance: 这是一篇值得精读的优化理解论文。它的贡献不在于给出一个新的训练 recipe，而在于把 Muon 的作用从“单步谱归一化”推进到“整条优化轨迹”的解释。对预训练研究的影响比较直接：Muon 可能更像早期探索优化器，而不是全程替代 AdamW/GD 的通用选择。这个结论会影响 optimizer switching、cooldown、late-stage refinement 和学习率 schedule 设计。对于正在尝试 Muon、Muon+AdamW 混合训练或矩阵感知优化器的大模型团队，这篇论文提供了一个更清楚的失败模式：Muon 的常幅度谱更新能快速沿 valley 探索，但靠近最优点时可能妨碍精细收敛。
summary.technical_approach: 作者先抽象出简化 Muon，去掉 momentum 和 Newton-Schulz 实现细节，只保留核心操作：对矩阵梯度取 polar factor，也就是保留奇异方向、丢弃奇异值大小。这样可以隔离“梯度正交化”本身的影响。分析模型选用 Burer-Monteiro factorized matrix sensing，因为该问题和二层 quadratic neural network 训练有联系，而且其梯度和 Hessian 结构可以由 sensing operator 精确控制。关键构造是 mixed-spiked matrix sensing：sensing operator 被分解为 signal、spike、bulk 三部分。signal 表示与 ground truth 对齐的任务相关各向异性；spike 表示任务无关但很强的各向异性；bulk 表示剩余近似各向同性方向。这个构造用来模拟 LLM 训练中常见的梯度谱结构：存在强 anisotropy，也存在长尾信息，但强方向不一定都是有用方向。随后作者采用 river-valley 视角分析 landscape。river direction 对应朝向 ground truth 的有效进展，hill directions 是横向偏离，通常更尖锐。GD 和 Muon 的差异在这个几何图像中变得清楚：GD 会快速从 hillside 落入 river，但进入 river 后沿有效方向推进变慢；Muon 能沿 valley 侧面更快移动，增强探索，但由于更新幅度被谱归一化，靠近最优点时不容易做小步精修。
summary.experiments: 全文片段显示作者会在简化 Muon 之外验证部分发现，并用 Figure 3 展示深度学习训练中的梯度谱各向异性。核心现象是：在 mixed-spiked matrix sensing 的 river-valley landscape 中，GD 的轨迹更适合最终高精度收敛，Muon 的轨迹更适合早期快速探索；常步长 Muon 可能在最优点附近出现收敛困难。文中给出的描述没有包含具体 LLM 预训练规模、token 数、模型参数量或 Muon 相对 AdamW 的百分比提升，因此不能把结论解读为某个固定 recipe 的实测胜出。更稳妥的读法是：该论文为“早期 Muon、后期 GD/AdamW 类 refinement”提供理论动机，也解释了为什么 Muon 在实际 LLM 训练中常表现出 schedule-sensitive 的特征。
summary.reading_guide: 建议精读，预计 60–90 分钟。先看 Introduction 的问题设定，尤其是 Muon 正面理论叙事和 LLM 训练中混合实证表现之间的张力。然后细读 mixed-spiked matrix sensing 的定义，确认 signal、spike、bulk 三部分分别代表什么；这是整篇论文能否类比 LLM 训练的关键。接着看 river-valley decomposition，重点关注 river direction、hill directions 与优化轨迹的关系。图 1 和图 2 应该作为主线阅读：它们给出 GD 与 Muon 在 valley 中运动方式的差异。Figure 3 可用于连接真实训练中的梯度谱现象。最后重点看作者是否给出 optimizer switching 或 late-stage refinement 的实验验证；这部分最接近预训练 recipe 的可操作启发。需要保持一个边界：matrix sensing 是受控模型，不等价于 Transformer 预训练，但它能把 Muon 的优势区间和失败区间讲得比较清楚。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper studies why Muon can help LLM training in some regimes but fails to be uniformly better than Adam-like optimizers. Prior explanations emphasize spectral normalization and improved conditioning: Muon orthogonalizes matrix gradients, preserves singular directions, and discards singular values. The empirical picture is less clean. Gains are mixed, schedule-sensitive, and often stage-dependent. The central question is which parts of the optimization trajectory Muon improves and where its update rule becomes limiting.
summary_en.importance: This is a useful paper for pretraining researchers because it reframes Muon as a trajectory-level optimizer rather than a universally better replacement for AdamW or GD. The main implication is practical: Muon may be better suited to early exploration, while a GD-like or AdamW-like optimizer may be preferable for late-stage refinement. That matters for optimizer switching, cooldown design, late training stability, and hybrid Muon/AdamW recipes. The paper also identifies a concrete failure mode: the constant-magnitude spectral update can move efficiently along a valley but can obstruct precise convergence near the optimum.
summary_en.technical_approach: The authors first isolate a simplified Muon update by removing momentum and Newton-Schulz implementation details. The remaining operation replaces each matrix gradient by its polar factor, keeping singular directions while removing singular values. This isolates the effect of gradient orthogonalization. The theoretical testbed is Burer-Monteiro factorized matrix sensing, which is connected to training two-layer quadratic neural networks and allows the gradient and Hessian geometry to be controlled through the sensing operator. The key model is mixed-spiked matrix sensing. Its sensing operator decomposes into signal, spike, and bulk components. The signal component is task-relevant anisotropy aligned with the ground truth. The spike component is strong but task-irrelevant anisotropy. The bulk component captures the remaining more isotropic directions. This construction mirrors a common feature of LLM training: gradients are highly anisotropic, but not every dominant direction is useful. The authors then analyze the landscape using a river-valley decomposition. The river direction corresponds to meaningful progress toward the ground truth, while hill directions capture sharp transverse deviations. In this geometry, GD quickly descends from the hillside into the river but then makes slow progress along the river. Muon moves rapidly along the sides of the valley, which improves exploration, but its normalized update can prevent fine convergence near the solution.
summary_en.experiments: The provided text indicates that the authors validate some findings beyond the simplified Muon setting and use Figure 3 to illustrate spectral anisotropy in deep learning gradients. The main reported phenomenon is qualitative but important: in the mixed-spiked matrix sensing landscape, GD is better aligned with eventual high-accuracy convergence, while Muon is better at early-stage movement and exploration. With constant step sizes, Muon can have convergence difficulties near the optimum. The visible text does not provide exact LLM-scale training runs, model sizes, token counts, or percentage improvements over AdamW. The result should therefore be read as a theoretical and mechanistic explanation for schedule sensitivity, not as a fixed production training recipe.
summary_en.reading_guide: Read carefully in about 60–90 minutes. Start with the Introduction to understand the mismatch between the positive spectral-conditioning narrative around Muon and the mixed empirical behavior in LLM training. Then study the definition of mixed-spiked matrix sensing; the signal, spike, and bulk decomposition is the core abstraction. Next, focus on the river-valley decomposition and how it maps optimizer trajectories into river and hill directions. Figures 1 and 2 should be read as the main geometric explanation of why GD and Muon behave differently. Figure 3 is useful for connecting the controlled model to real gradient spectra in deep learning. The most practically relevant part is any validation of optimizer switching or late-stage refinement. The boundary is also important: matrix sensing is not Transformer pretraining, but it gives a clean explanation of why Muon can be useful early and problematic late.

recommendation.zh: 修正了Muon普适优于Adam的错误认知，河谷视角可直接指导预训练优化器选型与schedule设计，重点看§3的模型假设与LLM场景适配部分
recommendation.en: Corrects the misconception that Muon universally outperforms Adam; the river-valley framework directly guides pretraining optimizer selection and schedule design, focus on §3 model assumptions and LLM adaptation

summary_en.core_problem: The paper asks how to perform fine-grained selective parameter updates in stochastic optimization while keeping momentum optimizers plug-and-play and theoretically analyzable.
summary_en.importance: The contribution is an optimizer-side update policy. It tries to turn selective updates from task-specific or intra-layer heuristics into a general mechanism compatible with AdamW, Lion, and Muon. Its relevance to LLM pretraining depends on whether the effect survives realistic-scale training, throughput constraints, and loss-stability checks.
summary_en.technical_approach: MGUP applies a larger step size to a fixed selected proportion of parameters at each iteration, while the remaining parameters still receive smaller non-zero updates. The policy is layered on top of momentum-based optimizers, yielding MGUP-AdamW, MGUP-Lion, and MGUP-Muon. The paper also gives convergence guarantees for MGUP-AdamW without weight decay under standard stochastic optimization assumptions.
summary_en.experiments: The abstract reports experiments on MAE pretraining, LLM pretraining, and other tasks, but the provided text does not specify model scale, token budget, baseline recipe, effect size, or stability statistics. The main thing to verify in the full paper is whether the LLM result is a small proxy or a recipe-level signal.

recommendation.zh: 扫算法和 LLM 预训练表即可；选择性步长有意思，但没看到大规模干净 ablation 前，不该动 AdamW/Muon recipe。
recommendation.en: Skim the algorithm and the LLM pretraining table; selective step sizing is interesting, but without clean large-scale ablations it should not replace an AdamW/Muon recipe.

summary_en.core_problem: The paper asks when different Schatten-p norm geometries should be used in deep learning optimization, especially in regimes where Muon-like Schatten-∞ optimizers show mixed empirical behavior.
summary_en.importance: This is a pretraining optimization and training-dynamics contribution. It is directly relevant to LLM training because it analyzes Muon-style optimizers, warmup, large-batch preference, and Chinchilla-like scaling regimes under one geometric framework.

paper.title: Muon$^p$: Muon with Fractional Spectral Powers
paper.abstract: Muon is an increasingly widely used optimizer that replaces a gradient $G=USV^\top$ with its polar factor $UV^\top$, thereby flattening the singular spectrum. However, full flattening discards singular-value information that may matter for adaptation. We introduce Muon$^p$, a Muon-style optimizer that instead uses fractional spectral-power updates $US^pV^\top$ for rational $p\in(0,1)$, interpolating between Muon and gradient descent. To make it practical, we prove that fractional spectral powers

summary.core_problem: Muon 把梯度矩阵 G=USV^T 替换成极分解方向 UV^T，等价于把所有奇异值压平成 1。这个做法能平衡不同奇异方向的更新，但也会丢掉奇异值大小携带的适应性信息。Muon^p 试图解决的问题是：能否保留 Muon 的矩阵级谱归一化优势，同时不过度抹平梯度谱结构。
summary.importance: 这项工作对预训练和微调优化器研究有直接参考价值。它把 Muon 从一个固定的极分解更新扩展成一族谱几何更新：US^pV^T，p 位于 0 到 1 之间。p=0 接近 Muon，p=1 接近普通梯度方向。这个连续插值使优化器可以按训练阶段选择不同的谱偏置。对大模型训练来说，关键启发不是“换一个优化器超参”，而是把矩阵梯度的奇异谱当作可调的学习率分配对象：强压平有利于均衡学习，保留部分谱信息有利于适应任务结构。作者也指出 Muon^p 更偏向微调收益，而不一定在所有预训练阶段优于 Muon，这个限制很重要。
summary.technical_approach:
方法核心是用 fractional spectral power 更新替代 Muon 的 polar factor 更新。给定 G=USV^T，Muon 使用 UV^T；Muon^p 使用 US^pV^T，其中 p 是 0 到 1 之间的有理数。理论上，作者证明 US^pV^T 是 Schatten-q 范数约束下的最速下降方向，q=1+1/p。这给了更新规则一个几何解释：不同 p 对应不同的矩阵范数几何，也对应不同的谱方向重加权。

实现难点在于不能直接做 SVD。Muon 的 UV^T 可以用 Newton-Schulz 这类只含矩阵乘法的迭代近似。作者证明，任意分数谱幂不能由固定的一元多项式迭代得到；原因是只对当前矩阵做一元多项式变换不足以同时保留原始奇异值与迭代状态。为此，作者构造低阶奇 bivariate recurrence，也就是同时使用原始矩阵和当前迭代量的双变量多项式递推。这样仍然只需要矩阵乘法，保留了 Muon 在加速硬件上的实现形态。工程上它接近 Muon 的一行替换，但数学上从 polar factor 扩展到任意 rational p。
summary.experiments: 可见内容显示实验主要覆盖微调场景，而不是把 Muon^p 宣称为通用预训练替代。作者报告 Muon^p 在多种模型上提升数学推理、代码推理、验证困惑度和下游任务表现，并分析了它不如 Muon 的情形。分析维度包括谱学习率适应、课程阶段和 effective-rank 动态。给出的摘要和正文片段没有暴露具体表格数值、模型规模和提升幅度，因此不宜补写精确数字。更稳妥的结论是：Muon^p 的收益具有训练阶段依赖性，微调中保留部分奇异值信息更有帮助；在需要强谱均衡的阶段，完全压平的 Muon 仍可能更合适。
summary.reading_guide: 建议泛读时间 30 到 45 分钟。优先看第 2 节的 Theorem 2.1、Lemma 2.2 和 Theorem 2.3。Theorem 2.1 说明为什么 US^pV^T 不是随意插值，而是对应 Schatten 范数下的最速下降；Lemma 2.2 解释为什么不能直接复用 Muon 的一元多项式迭代；Theorem 2.3 是工程可用性的关键。实验部分重点看不同 p 的曲线、微调与预训练或早期训练的差异，以及 effective rank 分析。真正需要深挖的是 p 的选择是否可以随训练阶段自适应，而不是固定成一个新的默认值。

summary_en.core_problem: Muon replaces a matrix gradient G=USV^T with its polar factor UV^T, which flattens the singular spectrum completely. This can improve balance across singular directions, but it also removes magnitude information that may be useful for adaptation. Muon^p asks whether one can keep the matrix-level spectral benefits of Muon while retaining part of the singular-value structure.
summary_en.importance: The work is relevant to optimizer design for large-scale training and finetuning. It turns Muon from a single polar-factor update into a family of spectral updates, US^pV^T with p in (0,1). The endpoints connect Muon-like full flattening and gradient-descent-like magnitude preservation. The useful idea for pretraining research is that singular directions can receive a controllable form of matrix-level learning-rate allocation. Full flattening is not always the right bias; the preferred spectral geometry depends on the training regime. The paper is careful in this respect: the reported gains are strongest in finetuning, while Muon can still be preferable in regimes where aggressive spectral balancing is useful.
summary_en.technical_approach:
The optimizer update is defined as US^pV^T for a gradient matrix G=USV^T. The paper gives this rule a norm-geometric interpretation: for q=1+1/p, US^pV^T is the steepest-descent direction under a Schatten-q norm constraint. This connects the choice of p to an explicit matrix norm rather than treating it as a heuristic interpolation.

The implementation problem is the main technical point. Computing US^pV^T by SVD is too expensive. Muon avoids SVD for UV^T using Newton-Schulz-style matrix-multiplication iterations. The paper proves that arbitrary fractional spectral powers cannot be computed by a fixed univariate polynomial iteration. A recurrence must retain access to the original matrix as well as the current iterate. The proposed solution is a low-degree odd bivariate polynomial recurrence that approximates US^pV^T using only matrix multiplications. This keeps the hardware profile close to Muon and makes the change small at the implementation level.
summary_en.experiments: The visible content indicates that the empirical section focuses on finetuning. Muon^p is reported to improve math reasoning, code reasoning, validation perplexity, and downstream task metrics across several models. The paper also studies failure or non-beneficial cases through spectral learning-rate adaptation, curriculum effects, and effective-rank dynamics. Exact model sizes, table values, and improvement margins are not exposed in the provided text, so precise numbers should not be inferred. The safe empirical reading is that fractional spectral powers are most useful when preserving some gradient-spectrum information helps task adaptation, while standard Muon may remain better when stronger spectrum flattening is needed.
summary_en.reading_guide: A 30-45 minute skim is enough for most readers. Focus on Theorem 2.1 for the Schatten-norm interpretation, Lemma 2.2 for the impossibility of a fixed univariate iteration, and Theorem 2.3 for the practical bivariate recurrence. In the experiments, look for the sensitivity to p, the split between finetuning and other regimes, and the effective-rank analysis. The most interesting follow-up question is whether p should be scheduled or adapted during training rather than chosen as a fixed optimizer setting.

recommendation.zh: Muon 是否压谱过头是干净问题；只看算法递推、Schatten 解释和 billion-scale 消融。
recommendation.en: The clean question is whether Muon over-flattens the spectrum; read the recurrence, Schatten-norm interpretation, and billion-scale ablations.

paper.title: Zeta: Dual Whitening for Matrix Optimization via Coordinate-Adaptive Preconditioning
paper.abstract: Large-scale neural network training increasingly relies on matrix-aware optimizers that exploit the structure of weight parameters beyond element-wise adaptation. However, existing matrix-aware methods such as Muon have an underappreciated vulnerability: their core operation, Newton-Schulz iteration, depends critically on input conditioning, yet the raw momentum matrices exhibit severe coordinate-wise scale heterogeneity. In this paper, we first verify this scale heterogeneity through a chi-squa

summary.core_problem: Muon 这类 matrix-aware optimizer 依赖 Newton–Schulz 正交化来做谱白化，但原始 momentum 矩阵存在明显的坐标尺度不均。输入条件数差时，Newton–Schulz 迭代的正交化误差会变大，导致矩阵级更新方向失真。Zeta 要解决的是：在保留 Muon 矩阵几何优势的同时，先消除坐标尺度异质性，让谱白化有更合适的输入。
summary.importance: 这篇工作对预训练优化器研究有直接参考价值。它没有把 Muon、AdamW/AdaFactor 式坐标自适应看成互斥路线，而是把二者拆成两个顺序相关的预条件步骤：先做坐标白化，再做谱白化。这个视角对大模型训练有用，因为当前 optimizer 的改进常常在 element-wise adaptation 和 matrix orthogonalization 之间二选一，Zeta 给出了一个更清楚的故障模式：矩阵正交化之前的尺度分布会影响更新质量。贡献量级更偏向训练 recipe 和优化器机制改进，而不是新的预训练范式。
summary.technical_approach: Zeta 的核心流程是双白化。第一步是 coordinate whitening：用每个坐标的运行二阶矩对 momentum 逐元素归一化，相当于近似的对角预条件，目标是压平行、列或坐标上的能量差异。第二步是 spectral whitening：在经过坐标归一化的矩阵上执行 Newton–Schulz 迭代，将奇异值拉平，产生接近正交约束的矩阵更新。关键点在顺序：论文认为先谱白化再坐标归一化不是等价选择，因为 Newton–Schulz 对输入条件数敏感；只有先降低坐标尺度不均，后续的谱白化才更稳定。理论部分给出三个支撑：coordinate whitening 可解释为近似 diagonal preconditioner；该预条件改善输入条件数，从而降低 Newton–Schulz 的正交化误差；RMS scaling 不改变主要谱方向，避免白化过程破坏矩阵更新的几何结构。
summary.experiments: 论文先用 Transformer 中代表性权重矩阵的 row energy 做 chi-square uniformity test，检验矩阵内部尺度是否均匀。原始 momentum 的 p-value 在多层中持续偏小，说明行能量分布明显不均；coordinate whitening 后 p-value 明显向 1 移动，说明尺度不均被缓解。训练实验覆盖语言模型预训练的 0.6B 到 8B 参数规模，也包含 MoE 架构和视觉任务。对比对象包括 AdamW、Muon 和 AdaMuon。给出的总体结论是，Zeta 在收敛速度和下游性能上稳定匹配或优于这些基线。由于提供内容没有展开具体 benchmark 表格和数值，精确提升幅度不宜外推。
summary.reading_guide: 泛读建议用 20–30 分钟。优先看三处：第一，Introduction 中对 Muon 故障模式的描述，尤其是 Newton–Schulz 对输入 conditioning 的依赖；第二，chi-square uniformity test 的设置和 Figure 1，它决定了问题是否真实存在；第三，Theorem 1–3，对应 coordinate whitening 的预条件解释、条件数改善和谱方向保持。实验部分重点看 0.6B–8B 语言模型预训练曲线，而不是视觉任务结果。真正值得深挖的是 coordinate whitening 与 AdamW 二阶矩估计之间的关系，以及 Zeta 在 embedding、norm、bias、attention projection、MLP projection 等不同参数类型上的适用边界。

summary_en.core_problem: Muon-style matrix-aware optimizers rely on Newton–Schulz orthogonalization for spectral whitening, but raw momentum matrices can have strong coordinate-wise scale imbalance. Poorly conditioned inputs make Newton–Schulz less accurate and can distort the matrix update direction. Zeta addresses this mismatch by normalizing coordinate scales before applying spectral whitening.
summary_en.importance: The paper is relevant to pretraining optimizer design. Its useful contribution is not just another optimizer variant, but a clearer decomposition of two adaptation mechanisms: element-wise statistical stabilization and matrix-level spectral control. Instead of treating Adam-like coordinate adaptation and Muon-like orthogonalization as competing choices, Zeta makes them sequential. This is a practical observation for large model training, where optimizer changes often fail because an operation that is sound geometrically is applied to badly scaled training signals.
summary_en.technical_approach: Zeta applies a two-stage whitening pipeline. The first stage performs coordinate whitening by dividing the momentum entries by running second-moment estimates, giving an approximate diagonal preconditioner. This reduces coordinate-level energy imbalance. The second stage performs spectral whitening with Newton–Schulz iteration, equalizing singular values and producing an orthogonalized matrix update. The ordering is the main design choice: spectral whitening is sensitive to conditioning, so it should operate on a statistically stabilized matrix rather than raw momentum. The theory supports this view in three steps: coordinate whitening behaves like diagonal preconditioning under standard assumptions; the preconditioned matrix has a better condition number, reducing Newton–Schulz orthogonalization error; RMS scaling preserves the spectral direction rather than replacing the matrix geometry with a purely element-wise update.
summary_en.experiments: The paper first validates the failure mode with a chi-square uniformity test on row energies of representative Transformer weight matrices. Raw momentum matrices show consistently small p-values across layers, indicating strong intra-matrix scale imbalance. After coordinate whitening, the p-values move toward 1, suggesting that the imbalance is substantially reduced. The training experiments cover language model pretraining from 0.6B to 8B parameters, mixture-of-experts models, and vision tasks. Baselines include AdamW, Muon, and AdaMuon. The reported outcome is that Zeta matches or improves convergence speed and downstream performance across these settings. The provided content does not include exact benchmark tables or numerical gains, so precise effect sizes should be checked in the experimental section.
summary_en.reading_guide: A 20–30 minute skim is enough for the main idea. Focus on the Introduction for the identified Muon failure mode, especially the conditioning sensitivity of Newton–Schulz; inspect the chi-square test and Figure 1 to see whether scale heterogeneity is empirically convincing; then read Theorems 1–3 for the intended optimizer interpretation. In the experiments, prioritize the 0.6B–8B language model pretraining curves over the vision results. A deeper read should examine how Zeta handles different parameter classes, such as embeddings, normalization parameters, attention projections, and MLP matrices.

recommendation.zh: Muon 系优化器的失败归因值得看，先读 chi-square 诊断和 ablation；若规模实验干净，应进内部 optimizer sweep。
recommendation.en: The Muon failure diagnosis is worth checking; read the chi-square analysis and ablations, and reproduce it in internal optimizer sweeps if scale experiments are clean.

paper.title: LoRA-Muon: Spectral Steepest Descent on the Low-Rank Manifold
paper.abstract: Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) significantly reduces compute and memory costs for finetuning Deep Learning models but is often harder to tune than dense training: when using factor-wise optimizers such as AdamW, it is sensitive to initialization choices, its optimal learning rates transfer poorly across ranks, and it often fails to beat dense baselines. We derive LoRA-Muon by applying the Muon optimizer's spectral steepest-descent rule to the low-rank setting. Along with our split weight-decay rule,

summary.core_problem: 现有LoRA微调使用AdamW等因子级优化器时，对初始化敏感、最优学习率跨秩迁移差、性能经常无法超过全参数微调基线
summary.importance: 提出首个针对低秩流形的谱最速下降优化器LoRA-Muon，属于优化器方法创新，解决了LoRA微调的核心工程痛点
summary.technical_approach: 将Muon优化器的谱最速下降规则迁移到低秩设置，配合拆分权重衰减规则，作为全秩Muon/Shampoo系列优化器的低秩代理；设计保证最优学习率可跨秩、宽度、深度、因子缩放迁移
summary.experiments: 在TinyShakespeare数据集上开展计算匹配的对比实验：秩2 LoRA-Muon可恢复全秩训练的最优学习率；秩32 LoRA-Muon的种子平均验证损失低于全参数AdamW基线；同时验证Spectron优化器依赖任意因子缩放的缺陷

summary_en.core_problem: When using factor-wise optimizers like AdamW for LoRA fine-tuning, the method is sensitive to initialization, optimal learning rates transfer poorly across ranks, and performance often fails to outperform full-rank fine-tuning baselines.
summary_en.importance: Proposes LoRA-Muon, the first spectral steepest descent optimizer on the low-rank manifold, belonging to optimizer methodological innovation and solving core engineering pain points of LoRA fine-tuning.
summary_en.technical_approach: Adapts Muon optimizer's spectral steepest descent rule to the low-rank setting, paired with a split weight decay rule, serving as a low-rank proxy for full-rank Muon/Shampoo family optimizers; the design ensures optimal learning rates transfer across rank, width, depth, and factor rescaling.
summary_en.experiments: Compute-matched comparative experiments on TinyShakespeare dataset: rank-2 LoRA-Muon recovers the optimal learning rate of full-rank training; rank-32 LoRA-Muon achieves lower seed-averaged validation loss than full-rank AdamW baseline; also verifies the defect that Spectron optimizer relies on arbitrary factor scaling.

recommendation.zh: LoRA优化的核心突破，学习率跨秩迁移的结论可直接用于内部微调实验，重点看§3的谱下降推导和§4的对比结果
recommendation.en: Core breakthrough in LoRA optimization; the cross-rank learning rate transfer conclusion can be directly applied to internal fine-tuning experiments, focus on §3 spectral descent derivation and §4 comparative results.

paper.title: Muon Learns More Robust and Transferable Features than Adam
paper.abstract: Muon has recently emerged as a state-of-the-art optimizer for pretraining Large Language Models (LLMs) and vision classifiers. Despite its efficiency advantage over Adam and SGD, the feature-learning advantage of Muon remains unclear. This paper investigates Muon's feature-learning advantage through the lens of robustness and transferability. First, by evaluating pretrained models on corrupted images and texts, we show that features learned by Muon are consistently more robust than those learned

summary.core_problem: 这篇工作想回答一个在优化器讨论里一直悬而未决的问题：Muon 相比 Adam 不只是更省步数或更稳，它是否真的学到了更鲁棒、也更可迁移的表征。
summary.importance: 对预训练研究员的价值不在于又多了一个优化器，而在于它试图把优化器差异从“训练 loss/吞吐”推进到“表征质量”。如果结论站得住，优化器选择就不只是工程配方问题，而会影响预训练特征的下游寿命、鲁棒性和迁移效率，属于训练 recipe 层面的有用信号。
summary.technical_approach: 方法上不是提出新优化器，而是对 Muon、Adam、SGD 做表征层面的对比分析。作者从两个角度测量：一是对图像和文本扰动数据的鲁棒性评估，二是用线性探针和全量微调测试迁移性。进一步，他们训练逐层 probe，观察不同层的 logit margin，主张 Muon 的优势体现在更大的层内分类间隔，这可能解释其更强的抗扰动和迁移表现。
summary.experiments: 摘要显示实验覆盖 transformer 和 CNN 两类架构，并同时在图像与文本上比较 Muon、Adam、SGD。评估包括 corrupted inputs 上的鲁棒性、从预训练参数出发的线性分类与全量微调迁移效果，以及 layer-wise probe 的 margin 分析。摘要没有给出具体模型规模、数据集名称和提升幅度，因此现阶段更像是一个值得核查 setup 干净度的分析论文，而不是可直接采纳的 recipe 结论。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper asks a question that optimizer papers often leave unresolved: beyond speed or stability, does Muon actually learn more robust and more transferable features than Adam?
summary_en.importance: Its value for pretraining researchers is not that it introduces yet another optimizer, but that it pushes the comparison from training loss and throughput to representation quality. If the claim holds, optimizer choice affects downstream feature lifetime, robustness, and transfer, not just engineering efficiency.
summary_en.technical_approach: This is an analysis paper rather than a new optimizer proposal. It compares Muon, Adam, and SGD through two lenses: robustness under corrupted image/text inputs, and transferability via linear probing and full fine-tuning from pretrained checkpoints. The authors also train layer-wise probes and inspect logit margins, arguing that Muon yields larger margins across layers, which may explain both robustness and transfer gains.
summary_en.experiments: According to the abstract, experiments span both transformers and CNNs, and cover image as well as text settings. Evaluations include corruption robustness, downstream transfer from pretrained parameters with linear heads or full fine-tuning, and layer-wise margin analysis. The abstract does not provide model sizes, datasets, or effect sizes, so this currently reads as a useful but verification-heavy analysis rather than a recipe you would adopt immediately.

recommendation.zh: 如果你在评估 Muon 值不值得进预训练主配方，这篇该看；先盯鲁棒性和 layer-wise margin 那几张表，结论有意思，但没有大规模 LLM clean setup 前别急着改 prior。
recommendation.en: Read this if you're deciding whether Muon belongs in the core pretraining recipe; focus on the robustness and layer-wise margin evidence, but don't update your prior until you see a clean large-LLM setup.

paper.title: Denoise First, Orthogonalize Later: Understanding Momentum in Muon via Spectral Filtering
paper.abstract: Muon has recently demonstrated strong empirical performance in large language model training, but the theoretical role of momentum in Muon remains unclear. Existing analyses of Muon either remove momentum to study spectral updates in isolation, or retain momentum without explaining why it improves empirical performance. Our work bridges this gap by showing momentum in Muon acts as a spectral filter. Under a structured signal-plus-perturbation gradient model, we prove that momentum suppresses per

summary.core_problem: 这篇工作要解释的是：Muon 里为什么 momentum 这么重要，以及为什么必须先做 momentum 再做 orthogonalization。已有理论大多把 Muon 的极分解/极化更新单独拿出来分析，或者保留 momentum 但只能给出收敛上界，结论往往还是“重 momentum 不一定有益”。这和预训练里的经验现象不一致：标准 Muon 明显依赖 momentum，而且把正交化放在 momentum 前面会变差。论文抓住的核心不是一般意义上的“加速”，而是矩阵梯度流里的谱结构稳定性。作者要说明，momentum 在 Muon 中首先扮演的是谱滤波器：它先压低扰动方向、保留持续存在的主信号方向，拉开 signal/noise 的奇异值间隔；随后正交化才有可靠对象可作用。如果先正交化，奇异值幅度信息被抹平，后续再做 momentum 已经无法恢复信号与噪声的可分性。
summary.importance: 对预训练研究的意义主要有三层。第一，它把 Muon 这类矩阵优化器里一个长期悬而未决的问题讲清楚了：性能提升不只是“正交化更新”本身，而是“先滤波、后极化”这个顺序。第二，这个解释直接关系到大模型训练 recipe。很多优化器设计会把归一化、投影、正交化、动量、预条件等操作视作可交换模块，这篇工作说明在矩阵更新里顺序本身就是机制的一部分。第三，它给了一个比收敛率更贴近预训练实践的分析视角：不是只看目标函数下降，而是看梯度矩阵的谱间隔、主奇异子空间稳定性、以及这些量如何影响后续更新可靠性。对做 optimizer ablation、训练稳定性诊断、以及理解 matrix-valued update 为什么在 LLM pretrain 中有效，都有直接启发。贡献量级上，它更像是对 Muon 机制的关键补全，而不是提出全新优化器。
summary.technical_approach:
技术路线分成理论建模、顺序比较、以及与预训练现象对齐三部分。理论上，作者采用 structured signal-plus-perturbation 的梯度模型，把每步梯度写成持续存在的低秩 coherent signal 加上均值为零、方差有界、并与信号正交的扰动项。这个设定的关键不是追求最一般，而是刻画预训练中常见的情形：有一部分跨 step 稳定存在的方向，对应可积累的学习信号；同时有高频、各向分散的噪声。

在这个模型下，作者分析三条 pipeline：标准 Muon 的 pre-polar，即先形成 momentum buffer M_t=βM_{t-1}+(1-β)G_t，再取 polar factor O(M_t)；Orthogonal-SGDM 风格的 post-polar，即先对每步梯度做 O(G_t) 再做 momentum；以及不带 momentum 的 polar-only。核心结论有两步。第一步，momentum 对原始梯度流起到谱低通滤波作用。由于 coherent signal 在时间上持续，动量累积会保留并放大这部分结构；而均值为零的扰动会在时间平均中被压制。结果是第 r 和 r+1 个奇异值之间的 gap 随有效窗口增大而拉开，top-r 奇异子空间更稳定。作者用定理和推论把这种“谱间隔扩大—子空间更可靠”的链条形式化。第二步，polar update 的性质决定了它只能保留奇异向量方向，不能保留奇异值大小。一旦对 noisy gradient 直接做 polar，信号与噪声在幅度上的差异被抹掉，后面再做 momentum 只能在已经失真的方向上平滑，无法重新建立谱分离。因此 pre-polar 优于 post-polar 不是经验巧合，而是由非交换性和信息保真顺序决定的。

论文还给出定量分离结果：在固定信号矩阵下，pre-polar 的更新方向与真实信号子空间更接近，post-polar 和 polar-only 会受到更大的扰动偏移。这里值得注意的一点是，作者不是简单说“momentum 降噪”，而是把降噪具体化为“为后续极化创造可辨识的谱结构”。这比传统 SGDM 分析更贴近 Muon 的特殊性。
summary.experiments:
实验部分的重点不是刷任务，而是验证理论预测和顺序效应。文中首先在预训练曲线上比较 pre-polar、post-polar、polar-only，结论很稳定：标准 Muon 的 pre-polar 全程优于另外两种变体，说明 momentum 既不能删，也不能随意换顺序。摘要截断前已经明确指出 Figure 1 展示了这一趋势；从引言叙述看，这个差距贯穿训练过程，而不是只在早期出现。

更关键的实验应当是围绕谱量展开：作者检查 momentum buffer 与原始梯度在奇异值分布、谱间隔、以及主奇异子空间对齐上的差异，验证“momentum 先扩大 gap，再让 polar 更可靠”这一机制。按全文结构，理论部分给出 Theorem 1、Corollary 1、Theorem 2、3，对应实验通常会展示：随着 momentum window 或 β 增大，M_t 的 top-r / tail singular separation 更明显；pre-polar 的更新与信号矩阵的夹角更小；post-polar 因为先把 singular values 全部压成 1，后续无法恢复这种 separation。引言还提到 heavier momentum 在旧理论里会恶化收敛上界，但实践中 Muon 受益于 momentum，这篇工作用谱分析解释了这个表面矛盾。

从你给出的全文片段里，没有完整保留具体参数量、token 数、或精确提升数字，因此不能编造数值。阅读时应重点去正文实验节和附录表格核对三类信息：一是预训练设置规模，二是不同 β 下的性能曲线，三是谱 gap / subspace alignment 的定量图。如果这些图和理论量一一对应，这篇工作的说服力会明显增强。
summary.reading_guide:
建议按“问题—机制—顺序—证据”四步读。先看 Introduction 里对三条 pipeline 的定义和 Figure 1，先把经验事实记住：pre-polar > post-polar > polar-only。然后直接读 Theorem 1 和 Corollary 1，对应的问题是 momentum 到底改变了什么；这里重点盯住两个量：spectral gap 和 top-r singular subspace stability。接着读 Theorem 2 和 3，看为什么顺序不能交换，尤其要理解 polar factor 会抹掉奇异值幅度信息这一点。最后再回到实验节，检查每个理论量是否有可观测 proxy 支撑。

精读时有三个值得深挖的点。第一，作者使用的 BVMZOS 扰动模型到底覆盖哪些真实训练噪声，哪些又不覆盖；这决定理论外推边界。第二，signal persistence 假设和预训练中的梯度时间相关性如何对应，是否能从真实 run 的 gradient covariance 里测到。第三，Newton–Schulz 近似误差在这个机制里扮演什么角色；如果正交化只是近似实现，谱滤波带来的收益是否仍然稳健。若时间有限，主文看引言、理论主定理、实验主图，再扫附录里的证明结构和额外 ablation，大约 45–60 分钟能抓住主线；若要用于 optimizer 研究，附录值得认真看。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper explains two tightly coupled questions in Muon: why momentum is empirically indispensable, and why it must be applied before orthogonalization rather than after it. Prior analyses typically isolated the polar update and removed momentum, or kept momentum only in convergence proofs that did not explain its practical benefit. That leaves a gap between theory and LLM pretraining practice, where standard Muon clearly outperforms both a no-momentum variant and an orthogonalize-first variant. The paper argues that the key role of momentum in Muon is not generic acceleration. It is spectral filtering on the matrix gradient stream. Momentum suppresses temporally incoherent perturbations while preserving persistent low-rank signal, thereby enlarging the singular-value gap and stabilizing the leading singular subspaces. Orthogonalization should then act on this denoised matrix. If polar normalization is applied first, it destroys the amplitude information that separates signal from noise, and later momentum cannot recover that lost distinction.
summary_en.importance: For pretraining research, the contribution is mainly mechanistic rather than algorithmic. It clarifies that Muon’s advantage is not just “orthogonalized updates,” but the ordered composition of two operations: denoise first, orthogonalize later. That matters because optimizer recipes in large-scale training often treat momentum, normalization, projection, and matrix transforms as modular components whose order is secondary. This paper shows that, for matrix-valued updates, ordering is itself part of the optimization mechanism. It also shifts the analysis target from classical convergence-rate statements to quantities that are closer to what matters in pretraining: spectral gap, singular-subspace reliability, and robustness of the update direction under noisy gradients. For anyone studying matrix optimizers, training stability, or why Muon works unusually well in LLM pretraining, this is a useful missing piece.
summary_en.technical_approach:
The technical setup combines a structured gradient model with a comparison of three update pipelines. Gradients are modeled as a coherent low-rank signal plus a bounded-variance, mean-zero perturbation that is orthogonal to the signal. This is a deliberate abstraction: it captures the idea that some directions persist across steps and should accumulate, while other components behave like high-frequency noise.

The paper studies three pipelines. Pre-polar is standard Muon: first form the momentum buffer M_t = beta M_{t-1} + (1-beta) G_t, then apply the polar factor O(M_t). Post-polar is the Orthogonal-SGDM style variant: first orthogonalize each step O(G_t), then apply momentum. Polar-only removes momentum entirely. The first main result is that momentum acts as a spectral low-pass filter on the raw gradient stream. Because the coherent signal persists over time, it survives temporal averaging; the zero-mean perturbation is attenuated. This enlarges the gap between the r-th and (r+1)-th singular values and improves alignment of the top-r singular subspaces of M_t with those of the underlying signal. The second main result is about ordering. The polar factor preserves singular directions but replaces singular values by ones. If it is applied directly to a noisy gradient, it erases the magnitude structure that distinguishes signal from perturbation. Momentum applied afterward can only smooth already distorted directions; it cannot recreate the lost spectral separation. Hence pre-polar dominates post-polar for structural reasons, not as an implementation accident.

A useful aspect of the analysis is that it does not stop at the vague statement “momentum reduces noise.” It specifies what kind of noise reduction matters for Muon: creating a matrix whose spectrum is sufficiently separated so that the subsequent orthogonalization acts on stable leading subspaces. That is the optimizer-specific mechanism.
summary_en.experiments:
The experimental goal is to validate the spectral-filtering story and the ordering effect, rather than to introduce a new benchmark result. The paper first compares pre-polar, post-polar, and polar-only in pretraining. The qualitative result is clear from the introduction: standard pre-polar Muon consistently outperforms both alternatives throughout training, showing that momentum is essential and that the order cannot be swapped.

The more informative experiments are the spectral diagnostics. The theory predicts that the momentum buffer should exhibit a larger top-r versus tail singular-value separation than the raw gradient, and that the leading singular subspaces should align better with the coherent signal. It also predicts that post-polar loses this advantage because orthogonalizing G_t first flattens all singular values to one. The full paper likely includes plots of spectral gap versus momentum strength or effective window size, subspace alignment metrics, and update-direction comparisons under controlled signal-plus-noise settings. Those are the figures to inspect carefully, because they connect the theorems to observable training behavior.

The provided text does not include complete numerical tables, model sizes, token counts, or exact performance deltas, so those should be verified directly in the experimental section and appendix. In practice, the most important numbers are not just end-task loss differences, but whether the measured spectral quantities track the theory across beta values and across the three pipelines.
summary_en.reading_guide:
Start with the introduction and the figure comparing the three pipelines. That establishes the empirical fact to be explained: pre-polar beats post-polar and polar-only. Then read Theorem 1 and its corollary first. The key question there is what momentum changes in the matrix spectrum: focus on spectral gap growth and stability of the top-r singular subspaces. After that, read Theorems 2 and 3 to understand why the order matters. The central conceptual point is simple but easy to miss: the polar factor keeps singular vectors but discards singular-value magnitudes, so applying it too early destroys the very information needed to separate signal from noise.

Three details are worth deeper inspection. First, how realistic is the bounded-variance mean-zero orthogonal perturbation model for actual pretraining gradients? Second, how strong is the signal persistence assumption, and can it be related to measurable temporal correlation in real training runs? Third, how does approximate orthogonalization via Newton–Schulz interact with the theory—does the mechanism survive implementation error? If reading for optimizer research, the appendix is worth the time. If reading for a quick mechanism check, the introduction, main theorems, and the spectral diagnostic figures should be enough in about an hour.

paper.title: MuCon: Clipped Muon Updates for LLM Training
paper.abstract: Muon-style optimizers take a matrix-valued momentum or preconditioned update $B = U \operatorname{diag}(σ_1,\ldots,σ_r) V^\top$ and replace it with its canonical partial polar factor $\operatorname{Pol}(B) = U V^\top$. This maps every nonzero singular value to one. MuCon is the clipped-Muon variant studied here: it applies singular-value clipping to the same Muon matrix, $D^{\mathrm{MuCon}}\_τ(B) = \operatorname{MClip}\_τ(B) = U \operatorname{diag}\bigl(\min\{σ\_i,τ\}\bigr) V^\top, \qquad τ> 0$.

summary.core_problem: 这篇论文解决 Muon 类优化器里的一个关键问题：polar Muon 会把矩阵更新的所有非零奇异值都变成 1，操作过于激进；是否可以只截断过大的奇异值，同时保留小奇异值中的幅度信息，并且让这个操作在大模型训练中有可实现的近似算法。
summary.importance: 这是一篇偏优化器基础构件的论文，对预训练的价值在于更新谱控制。Muon 的吸引力来自对矩阵更新方向做正交化，从而控制隐藏层矩阵的算子尺度；但 polar step 会丢掉全部奇异值大小，可能破坏优化信号。MuCon 把这个操作改成 spectral clipping：只限制谱范数，不抹平所有方向。这个改动更接近“约束更新大小”而不是“重写更新几何”。它与 SpectralP/CompleteP 这类宽度-深度联合缩放参数化连接紧密，目标是让小模型调参更容易迁移到大模型。
summary.technical_approach: 给定 Muon 矩阵 B_t 的紧 SVD B_t=UΣV^T，标准 Muon 使用 canonical partial polar factor UV^T，也就是把每个非零奇异值替换为 1。MuCon 使用 MClip_τ(B_t)=U min(Σ,τI) V^T，默认 τ=1。这个算子有一个干净的几何解释：它是把矩阵投影到谱范数不超过 τ 的闭球上，投影度量是 Frobenius norm。它也有低秩校正形式：只对超过阈值的奇异方向做修正，MClip_τ(M)=M-U_>(Σ_>-τI)V_>^T。因此，如果超过阈值的奇异值数量 k_> 很少，partial SVD、Lanczos 或 randomized subspace method 是自然选择；如果 k_> 很多，全局矩阵函数迭代可能更合适。论文还把 clipping 写成 polar/absolute-value 形式，指出阈值附近的特征值会带来数值不稳定，因为 clip 函数在阈值处不可光滑。最后，作者分析了用于 clipped positive-semidefinite factor 的 rational Newton iteration，并强调它只是 spectral filter，不是完整的免 SVD 算法。
summary.experiments: 给定材料主要是数学和数值算法分析，没有提供完整训练实验表。可确认的实验相关设定是：MuCon 被放在 SpectralP 参数化下讨论，隐藏二维矩阵参数组使用 Muon/MuCon 的谱控制更新，标量、向量、embedding、unembedding 等参数组仍使用 AdamW companion groups。SpectralP 的动机来自 CompleteP 的宽度-深度联合 scaling：希望 hidden matrix updates 的谱尺度可控，从而支持 hyperparameter transfer。文中没有可核验的模型规模、token 数、loss 曲线或下游性能数字，因此阅读时应把它视为优化器 primitive 和数值近似报告，而不是已完成的大规模训练 recipe 论文。
summary.reading_guide: 精读建议优先看 Introduction 中对 MClip_τ、MuCon、SpectralP 三者的区分。这一点很重要：MClip 是数学算子，MuCon 是把该算子放进 Muon pipeline 的 optimizer primitive，SpectralP 是隐藏矩阵参数组的缩放参数化。其次看投影定理和低秩校正恒等式，它们决定了近似算法该怎么设计。然后看 polar/absolute-value formulation 和 rational Newton iteration，重点不是公式复杂度，而是它为什么只能作为 spectral filter，以及阈值特征值为什么难处理。Background 的 CompleteP/μP 部分建议细读到学习率和 residual depth scaling 的规则，因为这解释了为什么谱控制更新与宽深缩放迁移有关。若只关心工程落地，重点检查后续是否有 partial SVD、Lanczos、randomized method 与 Newton-style filter 的实际开销比较。

summary_en.core_problem: The paper studies a core optimizer primitive for Muon-style training. Standard polar Muon maps every nonzero singular value of a matrix update to one, which is a strong intervention. MuCon asks whether one can instead clip only the singular values that exceed a threshold, preserve the remaining magnitude information, and approximate this operation well enough for LLM training.
summary_en.importance: The relevance to pre-training is update spectrum control. Muon is attractive because it constrains matrix-valued hidden updates through an orthogonalized direction, but the polar step discards all singular-value magnitudes. MuCon changes the operation from full polar normalization to spectral clipping. This is closer to constraining update size than replacing the entire update geometry. The connection to SpectralP and CompleteP matters because the intended use case is hyperparameter transfer under simultaneous width and depth scaling: tune small, train larger, while keeping hidden matrix update spectra under control.
summary_en.technical_approach: For a Muon matrix B_t with compact SVD B_t=UΣV^T, polar Muon uses the canonical partial polar factor UV^T, replacing every nonzero singular value by one. MuCon uses MClip_τ(B_t)=U min(Σ,τI) V^T, with τ=1 as the default. The operator has a clean variational meaning: it is the Frobenius projection of the matrix onto the spectral-norm ball of radius τ. It also admits a low-rank correction identity, MClip_τ(M)=M-U_>(Σ_>-τI)V_>^T, where only the singular directions above the threshold are modified. This identity gives the algorithmic split: when the number of violating singular values is small, partial SVD, Lanczos, or randomized subspace methods are natural; when many singular values violate the threshold, global matrix-function iterations may be competitive. The paper also derives a polar/absolute-value formulation and explains why eigenvalues near the clipping threshold are numerically delicate. Its rational Newton iteration for the clipped positive-semidefinite factor should be read as a spectral filter, not as a complete SVD-free optimizer implementation.
summary_en.experiments: The provided content is primarily mathematical and numerical-analysis oriented, and does not expose full training experiment tables. The confirmed training context is SpectralP MuCon: hidden two-dimensional matrix groups use the Muon/MuCon spectral update class, while scalar, vector, embedding, and unembedding groups remain AdamW companion groups. The motivation comes from CompleteP-style joint width-depth scaling, where controlled hidden-matrix update spectra are expected to help hyperparameter transfer. No verifiable model sizes, token counts, loss curves, or downstream metrics are available in the supplied text, so the paper should be treated as an optimizer-primitive and approximation report rather than a complete large-scale training recipe.
summary_en.reading_guide: Read carefully the early definitions that separate MClip_τ, MuCon, and SpectralP. MClip is the mathematical clipping map, MuCon is the optimizer primitive that inserts this map into the Muon pipeline, and SpectralP is the scaling parameterization for hidden matrix groups. Then focus on the projection theorem and the low-rank correction identity; these determine which numerical approximations are sensible. The polar/absolute-value formulation and rational Newton analysis are worth reading for their failure modes: the threshold is nonsmooth, and the Newton iteration is only a spectral filter. The CompleteP/μP background is useful because it explains why spectral update control is tied to width-depth hyperparameter transfer. For engineering use, the key missing evidence to look for is wall-clock cost and accuracy tradeoffs among partial SVD, Lanczos, randomized methods, and Newton-style filters inside an optimizer loop.
